Per predictas conclusiones intelligi potest, que sit omiomeria Anaxagorae, quam opi- fex intellectus distinguit.6 (Through the preceding conclusions one can understand what Anaxagoras’s homoeomeria is, which the demiurge of the intellect distinguishes.)7

draws from Simplicius’s In Aristotelis physicorum libros commentaria. The similarity of the two passages is obvious: Per predictas conclusiones intelligi potest, que sit omiomeria Anaxagorae, quam opifex in- tellectus distinguit.49 (Through the preceding conclusions one can understand what Anaxago- ras’s homoeomeria is, which the demiurge of the intellect distinguishes.)50
